local_checks.invariant: escapeHtml (admin.js:62) neutralises &, <, > and both quote characters, so its output is safe in element content and in quoted attribute values
local_checks.result: escapeHtml sets textContent and reads innerHTML, which encodes & < >, then replaces " with " and ' with '. Every attribute sink in the scope that takes text (title, value, data-*) is double-quoted, so the output cannot break out of the attribute.

local_checks.invariant: renderRich/renderInline/renderCell (admin.js:67-149, the same copy in app.js) escape all input before adding any markup and add no attributes built from input
local_checks.result:
renderInline calls escapeHtml first. The code, strong, [u] and [i] rewrites only wrap text that is already escaped in tags that have no attributes. renderCell turns back only the literal escaped forms of
and  . In renderRich, fenced code, labels, topics and example headings go through escapeHtml or renderInline. The only attributes are a class taken from a fixed DIFF map keyed by the regex group Easy|Medium|Hard, a fixed li-sub class, and
    built from parseInt, which is always an integer. The change from escapeHtml to renderRich(a.prompt) in showDetail (admin.js:1492) is therefore safe, including for resume-derived Part 2 prompts.

The total cell (1217) escapes manualTotalReason inside its title attribute. totalHtml (1503-1512) escapes manual_total_by and manual_total_reason. revokeDialog (1080) escapes name/email. tabBadge (1110-1113) escapes the title and runs the count through num. Deductions (1484), ai_reasoning (1495) and interview questions (1533-1537) are escaped.

local_checks.invariant: Values placed in HTML without escaping are server-typed numbers or server-generated IDs that no candidate or manager can set
local_checks.result: part1/part2_tab_switch_count (1436-1438, 1529) only ever change through SQL +1 increments (candidate-docs.ts:218, timer.ts:118,148). The writers pasteCount and pasteMax are COUNT(*) and MAX(chars), and chars is clamped by n() (candidate-docs.ts:215, admin-docs.ts:349-362). manual_total and manual_score are stored only after checks that the input is a finite number in 0.25 steps (admin.ts:1523-1524, 1556-1557). Candidate IDs, question_bank IDs and part2_questions IDs come from newId (db.ts:5-8, admin-docs.ts:141,201, admin.ts:852,1044, randomize.ts:306); part3 IDs come from the built-in bank. local_checks.invariant: Browser policy as a second layer behind the escaping

local_checks.invariant: Candidate text cannot leave the quoted answer block or pose as grader context. The only candidate-controlled inputs to the writers grading prompt are the answer text and the Part 2 paste and typing numbers.
local_checks.result: gradeWritingAnswer (openai.ts:460-472) creates a fresh boundary, ANSWER-<crypto.randomUUID()>, for every call. It removes any copy of that boundary from the answer (split(boundary).join('')) and sends system and user as separate typed roles in chatJson (openai.ts:45-48), so there is no candidate-controlled role field. The question prompt, model answer, guidance, copyNote, word count and paste evidence are built server-side and placed outside the boundary (openai.ts:461-467). The paste and typing numbers come from attempt_events, which logEvent (candidate-docs.ts:211-215) clamps to integers, so they cannot carry text into the prompt. Prompt-injection text still sits inside the intact boundary. Any effect on the candidate's own marks is a guardrail matter with no code-level boundary failure, so it is not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: Model output becomes marks only after deterministic bounding, and is written only while this grading run still holds the candidate's claim.
local_checks.result: The model's score and its deductions are reconciled by taking the lower of the two. The score is snapped to quarter marks and clamped to [0, maxMarks], where maxMarks comes from the DB question or part2_questions marks, which the triggers keep above 0 (openai.ts:475-486). Deduction marks are floored at 0 and deductions without a string reason are dropped. ai_content_percent is clamped to 0-100 and does not affect writers marks. Persistence in gradeDocsCandidate (admin-docs.ts:416-421, 439-444) uses bound parameters gated on the grading_claim. Resume and Retake drop the claim (admin-docs.ts:235, 253-255), and analysis/run and /grade release it on failure (admin.ts:1338-1343, 1380-1383). Re-grading leaves manual_score alone, so a manager's override keeps priority through COALESCE.

local_checks.invariant: The copy check (copiedFromQuestion, auto-zero and copyNote) is computed server-side and affects only the answering candidate's own marks.
local_checks.result: copiedFromQuestion (openai.ts:367-380) is deterministic and linear. It builds a set of the question's 5-word sequences, makes one pass over the answer, and is bounded by the 20,000-character prompt and the 100,000-character answer cap. The automatic zero applies only to Part 2, and only when at least 85% of the answer and at least 50 words are copied (openai.ts:419-425). Its inputs are the candidate's own answer and the manager-written prompt, so it cannot move another candidate's marks. Evading it, for example with homoglyphs, only hands the decision back to the model. That weakens a fairness heuristic but crosses no boundary (see hardening).

local_checks.invariant: Grader output cannot expose data the reader is not allowed to see, and grading context cannot leak between candidates.
local_checks.result: Each grading call is a stateless request containing one answer and that question's prompt, model answer and guidance (admin-docs.ts:405-438). There is no history, memory or cache. The model's reasoning goes only to admin views and the CSV. Panel members can already read reference_answer and rubric through GET /api/admin/questions, which is not manager-only (admin.ts:799-812; roles.ts:7-26 covers only the write routes). Candidate routes never return marks or reasoning (candidate-docs.ts:16-19, 318-320). No principal gains access to data across a boundary.

local_checks.invariant: When one candidate's grading fails, other candidates are not blocked and grading does not loop forever.
local_checks.result: chatJson does not retry hard 4xx errors (openai.ts:65-78, 96). analysis/run grades each candidate inside its own try/catch and releases a failed candidate's claim (admin.ts:1333-1345), so the rest of the batch completes. The client stops after two rounds with no progress (admin.js:1401-1402). The only effect of a persistently failing answer is that the same candidate gets re-graded once per round. That spend is small and bounded by the operator's clicks.

hardening_notes: The word limit is enforced only in the browser (app.js:110-114, 428). The server stores up to 10x the limit in characters (candidate-docs.ts:373). Both the client and the grader count words with /\s+/ (openai.ts:412), which does not match U+200B and similar joiners. Text joined that way therefore bypasses the client clamp, and the grader is told the answer has a few words when it has thousands. The impact is only on fairness of the candidate's own marks. Suggested fix: count words server-side with a Unicode-aware tokenizer such as Intl.Segmenter, or treat [\s\u200B-\u200D\u2060\uFEFF] as separators, and reject or flag answers over the limit before grading.

With word limits now up to 10,000, the answer cap is 100,000 characters. If those characters tokenize badly (rare CJK or astral characters), the prompt can exceed the model's context window. OpenAI then returns a 400, which chatJson does not retry, so that candidate's grading fails every time and the candidate is re-claimed in each Analyze round (admin.ts:1340-1343). Only the candidate's own result is affected. Suggestion: estimate tokens before calling the model, or truncate with a marker, and record a failure per answer instead of failing the whole candidate.

The candidate answer and heartbeat routes call request.json() on the whole body before applying answerCap (candidate-docs.ts:423, 432). This code is unchanged. Rejecting bodies over about 2x the largest cap, using Content-Length and a streamed read, would stop a signed-in candidate from forcing a near-platform-limit JSON parse into a shared isolate.

copiedFromQuestion and plainWords match only ASCII [a-z0-9] (openai.ts:353-359), so swapping in homoglyphs or accented letters defeats both the Part 2 automatic zero and the copyNote. Normalizing with NFKD and a confusables map before building the 5-word sequences would make this fairness heuristic sturdier. The model still sees both texts, so no boundary is crossed.

gradeDocsCandidate grades every Part 2 question at once with an unbounded Promise.all, up to 40 per candidate (admin-docs.ts:433), while Part 1 uses pool(…, 6). Reusing the pool would keep each request within the Workers subrequest and connection limits when managers configure large Part 2 sets.

The Part 2 grading prompt pairs the prompt copied into part2_questions at assignment time with the reference answer and guidance read live from question_bank (admin-docs.ts:426-431). If a manager edits a question after it is assigned, the stale prompt is graded against the new guidance. This is an integrity issue, not a security boundary.

local_checks.invariant: Only a manager can change support questions-per-type, and saved counts are whole numbers within limits that never drop below the number of pinned (required) questions
local_checks.result: src/routes/admin.ts:414-446 checks the manager role inline (line 415), and roles.ts:22 also lists the path as manager-only. The route accepts each count only as an integer from 0 to 20 (lines 418-424) with a total from 1 to 40 (line 426). It rejects a count below supportPoolCounts().required, which counts active, non-deleted required questions (supportconfig.ts:60-77). saveSupportCounts writes only the four fixed support_q_* keys through bound parameters. getSupportCounts clamps every stored or environment value with clampCount (non-finite or negative falls back; maximum 20; rounded). No path reaches the draw with a negative, fractional or non-numeric count.

local_checks.invariant: Each category's draw includes every pinned question exactly once, and pinned and optional questions never overlap
local_checks.result: randomize.ts:51-61 selects pinned rows with required = 1 (active, not deleted, ordered by created_at and rowid). It throws when a category has more pinned questions than its count. Optional questions come from pickLeastUsed(..., optionalOnly=true), whose filter COALESCE(qb.required,0) = 0 (line 146) excludes every pinned row, so the two sets are disjoint and a set has no duplicate question. ensureRequiredCol (db.ts:125-132) creates required as INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, and every support writer stores 0 or 1 (admin.ts:880, 963, 1045). The short-bank check at line 67 still applies.

local_checks.invariant: Revalidation of fingerprint src/lib/randomize.ts:assignPart1Questions:non-atomic-existence-check-duplicate-question-set: overlapping prepare and start calls cannot give one candidate two Part 1 sets
local_checks.result: The run-1 root cause is gone. The pinned-question change kept the fix. Each position is inserted through INSERT OR IGNORE ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (candidate_id, position) inside one env.DB.batch (randomize.ts:80-84). That is backed by PRIMARY KEY (candidate_id, question_id) (0001_init.sql:40-45) and UNIQUE(candidate_id, position) (0017). A losing overlapping batch therefore inserts nothing at positions the winner holds. candidate.ts:149-155 and 157-169 both call the same function. The only remaining variant needs the counts to change between two overlapping calls for the same candidate (a manager save inside that window); see hardening. The writers assignDocsPart1 uses a single whole-set statement with NOT EXISTS (candidate_id) (randomize.ts:269-273).

local_checks.invariant: Behaviour when configuration is missing or a pinned question changes outside Assessment length
local_checks.result: Missing environment variables and settings default each count to 0 (supportconfig.ts:27-37). Editing a question to required, toggling one active or restoring one (admin.ts:950-966, 972-989) does not recheck pinned counts against the saved counts. assignPart1Questions then throws for every new candidate start (randomize.ts:57-58). That is manager-caused unavailability with a descriptive error, not a crossing of any principal boundary. It is recorded as hardening.

hardening_notes: src/lib/randomize.ts:86-105: an overlapping assignPart1Questions call that loses still treats the overlap between the winner's stored set and its own picked list as 'chosen'. It then increments question_usage again for those questions, so rotation counts can drift. Use the batch's meta.changes (or compare positions) to detect a loss and skip bookkeeping.

src/lib/randomize.ts:80-84: the per-position NOT EXISTS guard (unlike the writers whole-set guard) lets a second overlapping call add positions beyond the first call's set if the support counts or pinned set change between the two calls. Use the whole-set WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM part1_assignments WHERE candidate_id = ?) form, as assignDocsPart1 does.

src/routes/admin.ts:950-966, 972-989: marking a question required, toggling it active or restoring it does not recheck pinned counts against the saved support counts (only /api/admin/assessment-length does, at lines 427-432). Over the limit, every new candidate prepare or start then throws (randomize.ts:57-58). Validate pinned counts in those routes too.

src/lib/timer.ts:60-75 with src/routes/admin.ts:1582-1595: a revoke that commits between requireCandidate's access check and startPart's UPDATE leaves the attempt started but unsubmitted with access_revoked=1, and the start response still returns the questions. Add AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM candidates WHERE id = ? AND access_revoked = 1) to the startPart UPDATE, or recheck after the start.

hardening_notes: The panel config sign-in keeps the row's role (admin.ts:155; auth.ts:251 returns row.user_role and ignores bcr). Since Access now lists the shared panel row with an ordinary 'Make manager' button (admin.js:515), one manager click gives every PANEL_PASSWORD holder manager rights. local_checks.invariant: Revalidation of talo/auth/bootstrap-admin-session-survives-credential-rotation: every session issued by a config credential stops working when ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD or PANEL_EMAIL/PANEL_PASSWORD changes, including the row-bound sessions added by 998ba8c
local_checks.result: A config sign-in always passes viaConfig to createAdminSession (admin.ts:326). That sets bc/bcr whenever configRole is non-null and throws if no tag can be computed (auth.ts:194-199). getAdminRole re-derives the tag from the current env for row-bound sessions that carry bc (auth.ts:247-250) and for legacy null-user sessions (auth.ts:255-257). The tag covers role, email and password (auth.ts:213-218). The row's own password is a random unusable value (admin.ts:158), and the device cookie only relaxes rate limits, so neither carries the old secret forward. The prior root cause no longer holds at HEAD. The regression tests at audit-round4.test.ts:51-75 cover both roles.

local_checks.invariant: Admin sign-in requires the correct password for the resolved principal; the config fallback requires an exact config-email match; sign-in limits are counted before the password check; the old session is replaced on login
local_checks.result: The row password is checked first (admin.ts:300). The fallback requires loginEmail === the configured email AND secretEqual on the secret (308-309), so a named-account email with a wrong password cannot reach the config path. adminSigninBegin counts and refuses before verification (296-297; ratelimit.ts:235-259). clearAdminSession runs before a new HMAC-signed token with a random nonce is issued (325-326), so there is no fixation. The `email = ? OR username = ?` lookup (285) can only collide through manager-chosen display names, and a collision yields that row's own role only after its own password verifies. Settled for lower-trust principals.

local_checks.invariant: A manager's Disable, Delete or Reset password on the shared panel account in Admin > Access revokes sign-in by holders of the old shared panel credential
local_checks.result: Not enforced. The `AND active = 1` filter (admin.ts:285) makes a disabled panel row invisible, so a holder of PANEL_PASSWORD reaches the config fallback (309). ensureConfigAccount then sets active = 1 for any existing row (154) or recreates a deleted one (157-165). After a manager-set password, the row password fails and the same fallback still accepts PANEL_PASSWORD. Only the ADMIN_EMAIL recovery behaviour is documented (998ba8c message, README.md:125, wrangler.toml:97-99) and tested (writers-bank.test.ts:197-204). Panel reactivation is neither documented nor tested. The Access UI offers Disable/Delete on this row with the text 'They will no longer be able to log in' (admin.js:516, 529). It is reported as candidate talo/auth/panel-config-signin-reactivates-revoked-shared-account.

hardening_notes: The panel config sign-in keeps the row's role (admin.ts:155; auth.ts:251 returns row.user_role and ignores bcr). Since Access now lists the shared panel row with an ordinary 'Make manager' button (admin.js:515), one manager click gives every PANEL_PASSWORD holder manager rights. Consider capping a bc-tagged session's role at its bcr, or making config rows' role read-only in Access.

Reset password on a config row calls unlockAdminAccount with `u:${id}` (admin.ts:588), but config emails are rate-limited under the `e:${email}` key (admin.ts:295), so the reset does not lift a pause on those accounts. This is functional, not a boundary issue.

ensureConfigAccount can dereference a null row (admin.ts:163-165, `row!.id`) when both the derived name and the `name (email)` fallback are already taken usernames. INSERT OR IGNORE is then skipped and the config sign-in returns 500. The trigger needs a manager-chosen username, so this is a robustness note only.

After ADMIN_EMAIL is changed, the previous main-manager row stays an active manager account (no bc check applies to row-password sessions). If someone had set an own password on it, that access persists. Document that the old row should be disabled in Access after handing over ADMIN_EMAIL.

local_checks.invariant: Each saved answer is capped by a size derived from a bounded word limit.
local_checks.result: answerCap is max(15000, wordLimit*10) (candidate-docs.ts:154-156). Its input is bounded to at most 100,000 UTF-16 code units, or roughly 300 KB of UTF-8, which is well under D1's per-row size limit. The word limit comes from four places, each bounded: question_bank.word_limit, limited by wordLimitIn to 50-10,000 (admin-docs.ts:50-54, 139-140, 160-161, 192-193); the runtime triggers (db.ts:140-150) and migrations-docs/0019; the env defaults, clamped to DOCS_LIMITS (team.ts:37-44, 90-91); and part2_questions.word_limit, which is copied from the bank. The slice at candidate-docs.ts:373 runs before the write. The save happens only after the question-ownership lookup and only while the part is open and before its deadline (candidate-docs.ts:331-347, 425).

local_checks.invariant: Answer storage cannot accumulate past a fixed number of rows per candidate.
local_checks.result: A save is an upsert on (candidate_id, question_id) (candidate-docs.ts:333-338), so every 30-second heartbeat overwrites one row instead of adding one. Each candidate has at most maxQuestions 40 per part (team.ts:41). Candidates must be on the email allowlist and signed in. Integrity events are capped at 300 per part (candidate-docs.ts:45, 207-209). Worst-case storage is (number of allowlisted candidates) x (assigned questions) x (cap). That figure is fixed by manager configuration, and no single candidate can grow it, so this is not a shared-resource exhaustion finding.

local_checks.invariant: The larger cap does not create work that is superlinear or that keeps running after a request ends.
local_checks.result: Saving is a single slice plus one bound SQL statement. The client limits words with clampWords and countWords, which split on the same /\s+/ pattern the server uses for counting (app.js:106-114, 428). Downstream, the cap feeds one grading call per answer, triggered by an admin, and copiedFromQuestion processes it in linear time. Nothing keeps running in the background after a request ends. Unchanged code parses the whole JSON body before slicing; that is recorded as hardening.

hardening_notes: The word limit is enforced only in the browser (app.js:110-114, 428). The server stores up to 10x the limit in characters (candidate-docs.ts:373). Both the client and the grader count words with /\s+/ (openai.ts:412), which does not match U+200B and similar joiners. Text joined that way therefore bypasses the client clamp, and the grader is told the answer has a few words when it has thousands. The impact is only on fairness of the candidate's own marks. Suggested fix: count words server-side with a Unicode-aware tokenizer such as Intl.Segmenter, or treat [\s\u200B-\u200D\u2060\uFEFF] as separators, and reject or flag answers over the limit before grading.

With word limits now up to 10,000, the answer cap is 100,000 characters. If those characters tokenize badly (rare CJK or astral characters), the prompt can exceed the model's context window. OpenAI then returns a 400, which chatJson does not retry, so that candidate's grading fails every time and the candidate is re-claimed in each Analyze round (admin.ts:1340-1343). Only the candidate's own result is affected. Suggestion: estimate tokens before calling the model, or truncate with a marker, and record a failure per answer instead of failing the whole candidate.

The candidate answer and heartbeat routes call request.json() on the whole body before applying answerCap (candidate-docs.ts:423, 432). This code is unchanged. Rejecting bodies over about 2x the largest cap, using Content-Length and a streamed read, would stop a signed-in candidate from forcing a near-platform-limit JSON parse into a shared isolate.

copiedFromQuestion and plainWords match only ASCII [a-z0-9] (openai.ts:353-359), so swapping in homoglyphs or accented letters defeats both the Part 2 automatic zero and the copyNote. Normalizing with NFKD and a confusables map before building the 5-word sequences would make this fairness heuristic sturdier. The model still sees both texts, so no boundary is crossed.

gradeDocsCandidate grades every Part 2 question at once with an unbounded Promise.all, up to 40 per candidate (admin-docs.ts:433), while Part 1 uses pool(…, 6). Reusing the pool would keep each request within the Workers subrequest and connection limits when managers configure large Part 2 sets.

The Part 2 grading prompt pairs the prompt copied into part2_questions at assignment time with the reference answer and guidance read live from question_bank (admin-docs.ts:426-431). If a manager edits a question after it is assigned, the stale prompt is graded against the new guidance. This is an integrity issue, not a security boundary.
